subject: Chemistry
title: Solutions: Chapter Introduction
summary: Soda fizzes when opened and the sea does not freeze at 0 °C: both are solution behaviour. The chapter covers concentration, Henry's and Raoult's laws and colligative properties.
keyPoints: A **solution** is a homogeneous mixture; the component present in the largest amount is the **solvent**, the dissolved one the **solute**.
**Molarity** = moles of solute per litre of solution; also molality, mole fraction, ppm.
**Henry's law**: gas solubility rises with pressure (p = K_H x); opening soda lowers the pressure, so CO₂ bubbles out.

**Raoult's law**: a non-volatile solute lowers the solvent's vapour pressure; **colligative properties** (boiling point ↑, freezing point ↓, osmotic pressure) depend only on the number of solute particles.

blocks.p: Salt water is a solution: water (the larger component) is the **solvent**, salt is the **solute**. The mixture is uniform throughout (**homogeneous**).

blocks.p: Soda is bottled under high CO₂ pressure. When it is opened the pressure falls, the gas's solubility falls, and the extra CO₂ escapes as bubbles. A non-volatile solute takes up part of the surface, so fewer solvent molecules escape and the vapour pressure is lower.

list: Depression of freezing point (sea water freezes near −1.9 °C).

blocks.p: All four depend on the **number** of solute particles, not on what they are.

quiz.explain: Colour depends on the solute's nature, not on the number of particles.
